solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Work unit given backing by illustrious French city

indicators.note: to be given backing is to be sent backwards, so these letters read from right to left

blocks.note: the erg is the unit of work in the old CGS system of physics
illustrious and noble both mean distinguished or of high rank

explanation.surface: Some work unit is being sponsored by a grand French city, as if a factory had civic backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given backing' reads like sponsorship but tells you to turn the physics unit round; the reversed unit then sits beside the word for illustrious.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenoble is a large city in the French Alps, capital of the Isère department.

clue.text: Handed over to host too much in dance

indicators.note: a host takes guests inside, so one piece welcomes another into its middle

blocks.note: past tense of give, to hand over
OTT is short for over the top, meaning excessive

explanation.surface: Someone giving a party served far too much during a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT, for 'over the top', is a standard shorthand for excessive; it sits inside the past tense of give, between its V and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A gavotte is an old French folk dance in moderate duple time, later popular at court.

clue.text: European broadcasting for a very long time

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for European
a programme being broadcast is on air, so on

explanation.surface: A European station has been broadcasting for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcasting means on the air, which gives the short word after the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immeasurably long period of time, or in geology a span of billions of years.

clue.text: Ring lecturer to register unknown branch of dentistry

blocks.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written
to log is to record or register
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: An instruction to phone a lecturer and sign up for an obscure dental specialism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a verb meaning phone, but it is the circular letter; a don is an Oxbridge lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Odontology is the scientific study of teeth, their structure and diseases, treated as part of dental science.

clue.text: Reportedly one departing for bar

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: someone who departs is a leaver

explanation.surface: Word has it that somebody is quitting in order to go to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' seems to be a pub the leaver is heading for, but it is a metal rod used to prise things.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid rod pivoted to move a load, and a crowbar is exactly such a tool.

clue.text: Endlessly awkward old South American cowboy

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: gauche means socially awkward or clumsy
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old South American cowboy who is forever clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The French-derived word for awkward loses its final E, then the abbreviation for old is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a horseman or herdsman of the Argentine and Uruguayan pampas, a South American counterpart of the cowboy.

clue.text: Part of church Liberal abandoned by mistake

indicators.note: something abandoned has been left behind, so that letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: a lapse is a slip or small error
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Part of a church that a Liberal left by accident, like a politician deserting a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By mistake' reads as 'accidentally', but mistake is the word to be shortened; the Liberal's abbreviation leaves it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess, usually vaulted, at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Cooked meats home help carved on lake

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British cleaner who works in people's homes
carved and cut both mean sliced
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A cleaner slicing up cold meats beside a lake, which suits the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is an old British word for a cleaning lady; in a down clue 'on' puts one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcuterie is prepared pork products such as ham, sausages and pâté, sold ready cooked or cured.

clue.text: Senior citizen’s long-standing form of rest

indicators.note: to give something a new form is to reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: something long-standing has been around a long time, so it is old
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pensioner's habitual nap, a long-established way of resting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'form of' turns the four letters of rest into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an informal word for an elderly person, the same as a pensioner.

clue.text: Father acting, not son? It’s a façade

indicators.note: not having something means it is removed from the word

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
an actor at work is on stage
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father who performs while his son doesn't; the whole thing is just a pretence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Façade' looks like a figurative put-on, but here it is the literal face of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's frontage is its front side facing the street, which is precisely what an architectural façade means.

clue.text: Vehicle protector is light, used around posh part of Canada

indicators.note: something put to use around another thing wraps it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a van is a vehicle
a cover protects what is beneath it
U means upper class, as in the old U and non-U distinction
taken as written
to light on something is to alight or land on it

explanation.surface: A car cover that is lightweight and upmarket, as sold in a smart corner of Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective about the cover, but it is the verb meaning to come down and settle, as birds do.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver Island is the large island off Canada's Pacific coast, part of British Columbia and home to Victoria.

clue.text: Showing amusement about wren’s initial chirping

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round another
the initial of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: tittering is laughing quietly, showing amusement
the opening letter of wren

explanation.surface: Someone giggling about a wren that has started to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: The wren's letter goes in after the first T of the laughing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Twittering is the light, rapid series of chirps that small birds make, so it is birdsong.

clue.text: Carefree attitude a nice cousin cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated soil is dug and turned over, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant relative has developed a breezy, relaxed outlook on life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' seems to describe how the cousin acquired the attitude, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Insouciance, borrowed from French, is casual unconcern, a lack of worry or anxiety.

clue.text: Possibly Hamish’s second country dwelling

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a cot is a small cottage, a poetic word for a rustic home

explanation.surface: A man called Hamish may own a second home in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is', so 'Possibly Hamish' is the definition; 'possibly' warns that Hamish is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamish is a typically Scottish given name, the Gaelic form of James, so a Hamish is likely a Scotsman.

clue.text: Gifted girl’s place at top? That’s open to question

indicators.note: in a down entry the top comes first, so these pieces sit above the other one

blocks.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, with the possessive S
to place something is to put it
gifted and able both mean talented

explanation.surface: Is a talented girl's place at the top of the class really deserved? Some doubt it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'Di's put' placed at the top of 'able', since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disputable can be argued about or challenged, exactly what open to question means.

clue.text: Greek character’s crumbling pen outside farm store

indicators.note: something crumbling is breaking apart, so its letters fall into a new order
one piece stands outside another, wrapping round it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a silo is a tower on a farm for storing grain

explanation.surface: A Greek person's decaying animal enclosure stands beside a farm silo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, the equivalent of the short E.

clue.text: Young bird stuck at first in trap on heather

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the preceding word
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a net is used to trap animals
the opening letter of stuck
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A baby bird is caught in a snare laid on the heather moor.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling is a name for heather that solvers meet often; in a down clue 'on' puts the trap above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestling is a bird too young to leave the nest, still being fed by its parents.

clue.text: A famous surgeon, one of the top people

blocks.note: taken as written
Joseph Lister was the Victorian surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A celebrated surgeon counts as one of the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the clue: 'A famous surgeon' is the wordplay and the rest is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An A-lister is a celebrity on the most sought-after list, one of the elite in society or entertainment.

clue.text: Daughter meeting Dickensian character’s skivvies

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A daughter encounters the servants of a character from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skivvies' is British slang for menial servants, not the American sense of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A skivvy is a British word for a lowly household servant, and a drudge does hard, dull, menial work.

clue.text: Refuse to go downhill

blocks.note: first meaning: to turn down an offer
second meaning: to deteriorate or worsen

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like someone unwilling to walk down a slope, but 'Refuse' and 'go downhill' are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both politely turning something down and gradually getting worse, as health or standards do.

clue.text: English Queen entertaining politician, or another monarch

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's royal cipher
an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: An English queen hosts a politician, or perhaps a king from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The MP goes between English and Queen; 'or' looks like a link word but supplies the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor rules an empire, so he is a sovereign ruler just as the Queen in the wordplay is.

clue.text: Artist on island framing publicity notice fast

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A painter on an island quickly puts a frame round a poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adverb for the framing, but it is the noun: a period of abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic holy month during which Muslims abstain from eating and drinking from dawn to sunset.

clue.text: Copy card game, briefly

blocks.note: first meaning: to copy someone else's work dishonestly
second meaning: a short form of the card game cribbage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' belongs to the second meaning only: it says the game's name is shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To crib is to plagiarise or copy, and crib is the everyday shortening of cribbage, a card game scored on a pegboard.

clue.text: Current cricketer’s runs welcomed by side

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a slip is a fielder standing beside the wicketkeeper in cricket, with the possessive S
a side is a team
R is the scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A present-day cricketer's runs are applauded by the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present-day, but it is a noun: a flow of air or water.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipstream is the current of air behind a fast-moving vehicle, which a follower can use to reduce drag.

clue.text: Model question

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who poses, as for an artist or photographer
second meaning: a puzzling or difficult problem

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like 'model question', a sample exam item, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who sits or stands for a picture and a baffling puzzle that is hard to answer.

clue.text: Spots in part of East London, as locals may pronounce it?

indicators.note: this points to how the word is spoken in a local accent rather than how it is written

blocks.note: Hackney is a borough of East London, and Cockney speech drops the H

explanation.surface: Someone notices blemishes around a district of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, the traditional working-class Londoners of the East End, famously drop their Hs, so the borough of Hackney comes out as 'Ackney.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, so spots on the face are its symptom.

clue.text: Unaware travellers in Aden born in Ascot, surprisingly

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is not the expected one, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Naive tourists in Aden turn out, unexpectedly, to have been born at Ascot.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is the link; the second belongs to the letters to be rearranged. Ascot is an English racecourse town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Innocents Abroad is Mark Twain's travel book about naive American tourists in Europe and the Holy Land.

clue.text: Mineral aggregate originally rife in outskirts of Odense

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter is used
the outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters are used
a piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Odense
the opening letter of rife

explanation.surface: Mineral deposits were once common on the fringes of the Danish city of Odense.
explanation.walkthrough: Odense is a city in Denmark; only its two ends are used, with one letter slipped between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ore is a naturally occurring mass of rock and minerals from which metal can be extracted profitably.

clue.text: Team assembled by the Spanish, no less

blocks.note: el is the Spanish word for the
even is used for emphasis, like 'no less' in 'the Queen, no less'

explanation.surface: A squad put together by Spaniards, no less impressively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team' is the definition because cricket and football sides have that many players.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side consists of that number of players, so the number itself names the team.

clue.text: Large plant seabird observed crossing sandbank

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so one piece stretches across and around another

blocks.note: a tern is a slender seabird
a reef is a ridge of sand or rock near the surface of the sea

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sees a seabird flying over a sandbank, with a large plant nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The seabird opens after its first letter to hold the sandbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree fern is a large fern with a tall trunk-like stem, growing to the size of a small tree.
